assets.describe: Elderly British military advisor, warm and wise, slightly gravelly, calm measured delivery, reassuring
assets.text: Welcome to the war table, Commander. Every general writes orders in secret, and every army marches at once.

assets.describe: Old grizzled field marshal, very deep gravelly voice, slow, stoic and commanding
assets.text: Marshal Varek. I have buried better generals than you. Let us begin.

assets.describe: Stern aristocratic woman general in her forties, cold, crisp, precise and commanding
assets.text: Lady Ysolde. I suggest you guard your doors.

assets.describe: Portly sly quartermaster, nasal and amused, quick merchant patter
assets.text: The Quartermaster, at your service. Everything has its price.

assets.describe: Young eager cavalry captain in his twenties, bright, boyish and overconfident
assets.text: Captain Oren! First war, but I am a fast learner!

assets.describe: Huge bearded northern warlord, booming deep voice, rough accent, laughs easily
assets.text: Old Bear Hask! Bring me your best, little general!

assets.describe: Calm sharp-witted woman tactician, low even voice, dry and understated
assets.text: Commander Imre. I have already read your plan.
Welcome to the war table, Commander. The world is wide, the maps are blank, and every inch of it is ours for the taking.
Plant our flag and pour in the troops. Spread too thin and the vultures will pick us apart.
Fresh regiments off the boats, Commander. Send them where the fighting is.
Select one of our lands, then click the enemy you mean to crush.
Careful. March them all out and that land stands empty. Any jackal next door could stroll right in.
We have regiments idling on the docks. Unplaced men go home, and I will not have it.
Orders sealed. Now we see who flinches.
There it is. Every army on the map, marching at once. Glorious.
A walk-in! They left the gates wide open and we marched straight through. Plant the flag!
Blast! They walked straight into a land we left empty.
Another land for the empire!
Our garrison held. Let them break their teeth on our walls.
We have lost ground there, Commander. We will take it back with interest.
The whole region flies our colours. Its riches will swell our ranks every round.
We hold a matching set of cards. Cash them in and call up the regiments.
Final round, Commander! Only land counts now. Throw in everything. Leave nothing in the barracks.
We lead the war. Every crown at this table wants our head. Let them come.
We are falling behind. Fortune favours the bold, Commander. Attack!
One less rival for the throne. Their lands are ripe for the taking.
We are beaten, Commander. Even empires fall. But what a war it was.
Victory! The world bows to you, Commander. Magnificent. Utterly magnificent.
Lands we hold dig in. Dug-in troops never march, so they keep a land safe while the rest go conquering.
A clean breakthrough! With men to spare, we can surge on to the next land.
Roll the dice, Commander.
The dice love us today!
Cursed luck!
Here is what I would do, Commander.
They are breaking! Press the attack!
Sound the retreat! Save the men for another day.
Send in the reserves! Every last man!
We are cut off, Commander. There is no retreat. Fight or die.
A bloody opening. Fall back now and save the men, or press on and pray.
A glorious opening! One more push and the land is ours.
The dust has settled, Commander. March the men up to the front before the next assault.
A melee, Commander! Every army piling in at once. Steady on every front!
Grand Marshal Varek. I have buried a hundred generals. You will be a hundred and one.
Advance. Fix bayonets. No quarter.
As expected.
A setback. They will pay for it in blood.
You left it empty. I merely accepted the invitation.
My war is over. Remember the old soldier.
The world is mine. It always was.
Fall back. Regroup. We return at dawn.
Bring up the reserves. End this.
Viceroy Ysolde. Every land at this table will fly my banner. Guard your doors.
Take it. Leave nothing standing.
Predictable.
You will pay for that. Dearly.
An empty fort is an insult to its owner. I have corrected it.
This is not the end of my house.
Kneel. The empire is mine.
Withdraw. For now.
Send everything. I do not lose.
Governor Quill, of the Company. Everything has its price, and I intend to buy the world.
An investment opportunity, lads. Go and collect.
Profit!
Hm. That will cost me.
Unguarded goods. Finders keepers.
Bankrupt. Well, it was lovely doing business.
Tally it up. The Company owns the lot.
Cut our losses, lads. Back to the ships.
Double the investment! Send the reserves!
Captain Oren of the Hussars! First war, but I have a very fast horse!
Charge! For glory!
Ha! Did you see that?
Wait, that was not supposed to happen!
Nobody home? Do not mind if I do!
I will be back. With more horses.
I won? I won! Somebody tell my mother!
Retreat! Tactical retreat! Very tactical!
Everybody! Everybody charge!
Commodore Hask, the Old Bear! Bring me your best, little general, and I will sink it!
Haaa! Break them! Burn their boats!
Hah! Soft as butter!
Grr. Lucky blow.
Empty? Then it is mine!
Bah! Pour me a drink. I am done.
The Bear rules land and sea! Ha ha ha!
Back to the ships! I will be back for you!
More! Send more! The Bear is hungry!
Admiral Imre. I have already read your plan.
Exactly as planned. Proceed.
Calculated.
Interesting. I will adjust.
You moved. I did not. That was the whole trick.
Well played. I underestimated you.
Checkmate.
The odds have turned. We withdraw.
Commit the reserve. Now.
